content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I understand it's possible to automatically shift the visible portion of the [product_name] display using the ticking option (every character or row), allowing access to hidden content. Is there a way to achieve this using the navigation keys (such as right or left keys)? Looking forward to your input. Thanks!
No, this can only be controlled through the setting in the message text. Texts on the display remain static except for the ticking feature; they cannot be moved using keys or other inputs.

[user_name] is correct regarding navigation within one screen. However, you can create multiple screens and switch between them using the cursor keys. I've implemented this often with [product_name] screens by assigning the F1 and F4 keys to select screens and using the F2 or F3 keys to adjust values within the currently active screen. Hope this helps!
Hi [user_name], Could you share the code you mentioned? I'm particularly interested in how to update display values using the up and down keys. Thanks a lot!

@ [user_name], please see the attached. This example shows a simple menu structure utilizing the [product_name] function keys, but you could also use other inputs. For clarity, inputs 1 and 2 can trigger the activation of different screens, enabling the same function keys to work as intended. I've used this setup in several projects. The idea for the menu structure isn't originally mine; I came across it elsewhere and have used it frequently, so credit goes to its originator. You will need to adapt it to suit your needs, but this approach allows for more flexible screen management. In one project (cannot share details for legal reasons), I used eight screens with similar content, making minor changes and triggering each screen using program steps to keep users informed about the process status.

analysis.insight_summary: The thread investigates how to navigate or scroll content on [product_name] screens beyond the built-in ticking option. Contributors point out that display texts are typically static except when ticking is enabled and recommend creating multiple screens navigable by function keys as a flexible workaround. Creative menu structures allow for improved user navigation, despite the built-in limitations.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking a way to scroll or move displayed content on a [product_name] display using physical navigation keys, similar to browsing additional data beyond the visible portion.
